title: Smaller image files: less decoded image memory, but not pixel-identical
problem: 45 photos on the page are stored much larger than they are ever drawn (for example a 480x480 avatar drawn 59 px wide on the phone, or a 1272x1272 service photo drawn 161 px wide on desktop). The browser decodes them at full size. Decoded at their natural size, these 45 images take about 95 MB. More decoded image memory makes it more likely that iOS runs short of memory under pressure and drops the page's smooth-scrolling layers. That is a risk, not something we have seen happen. This change does not make scrolling smoother by itself: it is insurance, not a frame-rate fix.
idea: Re-save the oversized images at a smaller size: at most 1.2x the largest size any of 9 screen sizes needs at 3x pixel density. Same file names, same format, the original JPEG quality (capped at 90), so nothing else on the page changes. Layout is unchanged: 0 image box differences over 9 screen sizes and 1204 image positions.
looksSame: At normal size the images look the same to the eye. In a whole-page comparison at 430x932, the A-vs-B difference is no larger than the difference between two loads of the unchanged page (the countdown and the animation phase).
risk: Pinch-zoom: zoomed in, the smaller files have less detail (softer at 1.2x the needed size, earlier than the original). The memory gain was measured only in the iPhone Simulator (2 sessions); the real phone was not measured. A future redesign that draws these images larger would need the originals again.

options.label: All 45 images
visualDiff: NOT pixel-identical. Per image, comparing the same spot with the old and new file in place:

Small round avatars in the commission section (28 px on the phone) are slightly softer: up to a 109 out of 255 difference on single pixels, on about 7% of the avatar's pixels (client-avatar-1; client-avatar-2 up to 92-103).
The seller avatars in the tabs (59 px on the phone) are slightly softer: up to 71 (web-developer), 48 (video-editor), 40 (two others), on 2-5% of their pixels.

Desktop-only service photos change in fine texture (grass, foliage, edges): up to 95 (sound-composer service-feature, 16% of its pixels above 8), 87 (service-ost), 80 (web-developer service-dd-transport), 54 (peter cover).
12 of the 45 files were never caught on screen by the per-image check (some reviewer avatars, two logos); 9 more were only seen where the unchanged page itself moves.

The same photo texture changes as option 1: up to 95 (service-feature), 87 (service-ost), 80 (service-dd-transport), 54 (peter cover), 44 (nam cover), 40 (leobeer cover); seen mostly on desktop.
6 of the 11 photos were only seen where the unchanged page itself moves, so their numbers are less certain.

options.idea: Change nothing. Write the result up (the Simulator saving is real but small and unproven on the phone) and keep the option of letting the browser choose a size per screen (srcset) as a later study.

recommended.why: Neither re-save option is pixel-identical, and your bar is no visible change. The gain is a memory reserve seen only in the Simulator (2 sessions); the phone has not run short of memory on this page. If small softening is fine, 'Large photos only' keeps ~2/3 of the saving.
